pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis ( secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma ) THE SMOKING GUN: The combination of acute psychiatric decline, continuous orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic instability, CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis, the EEG extreme delta brush pattern, and a pelvic mass identifying an underlying ovarian teratoma. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis is a severe autoimmune disorder characterized by pathogenic IgG antibodies directed against the GluN1 subunit of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor in the central nervous system. In young females, this condition is strongly paraneoplastic, triggered by ectopic neural tissue within a mature or immature ovarian teratoma. The binding of autoantibodies leads to cross-linking and selective internalization of NMDA receptors, resulting in a state of synaptic NMDA receptor hypofunction. This disruption of corticostriatal pathways initially manifests as psychiatric distress and psychosis, before progressing to movement disorders (dyskinesias), intractable seizures, autonomic instability, and central hypoventilation. Treatment requires prompt surgical resection of the teratoma alongside aggressive immunotherapy (high-dose steroids, IVIG, plasma exchange, and rituximab or cyclophosphamide).
